# Finding the Minimum Size of Set $A$

## Setting Up the Problem

I need to find the minimum $|A|$ such that there exists a function $f: \mathbb{N} \setminus A \to \mathbb{N}$ where $f(i) \neq f(j)$ whenever $|i - j|$ is prime.

This is a **graph coloring problem**: consider the graph $G$ with vertex set $\mathbb{N}$ where vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent if and only if $|i - j|$ is prime. I need to properly color $\mathbb{N} \setminus A$ using colors from $\mathbb{N}$.

## Testing $A = \emptyset$ (i.e., coloring all of $\mathbb{N}$)

I'll use a **greedy coloring algorithm**. Enumerate vertices in natural order: $1, 2, 3, \ldots$

**When coloring vertex $k$:** I must assign a color different from all already-colored neighbors of $k$.

A neighbor $j < k$ of vertex $k$ satisfies $k - j$ is prime. The set of such neighbors is:
$$\{k - p : p \text{ is prime},\; p < k\}$$

Since there are only **finitely many primes less than $k$** (exactly $\pi(k-1)$ of them, where $\pi$ is the prime-counting function), vertex $k$ has **finitely many** already-colored neighbors.

**Key argument:** Each of these finitely many neighbors has been assigned a specific color in $\mathbb{N}$. The set of forbidden colors is therefore **finite**. Since $\mathbb{N}$ is infinite, there always exists a color in $\mathbb{N}$ not used by any of $k$'s already-colored neighbors.

## Verification with a Small Example

| Vertex $k$ | Neighbors $j < k$ (where $k-j$ is prime) | Forbidden colors (finite) | Can assign a new color? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | none | $\emptyset$ | ✓ |
| 2 | none ($|2-1|=1$, not prime) | $\emptyset$ | ✓ |
| 3 | $j=1$ ($3-1=2$) | $\{f(1)\}$ | ✓ |
| 4 | $j=1$ ($4-1=3$) | $\{f(1)\}$ | ✓ |
| 5 | $j=2$ ($5-2=3$) | $\{f(2)\}$ | ✓ |
| 7 | $j=2,4$ ($7-2=5,\;7-4=3$) | $\{f(2), f(4)\}$ | ✓ |

At each step, only finitely many colors are forbidden, so a valid color always exists.

## Conclusion

The greedy algorithm successfully produces a proper coloring of the **entire** graph on $\mathbb{N}$ with no vertices removed. Therefore, no elements need to be excluded:

$$A = \emptyset \quad \text{works.}$$

Since $|A| = 0$ is the smallest possible cardinality of a finite set, the minimum number of elements in $A$ is:

$$\boxed{0}$$

27B·v4.method: Greedy coloring of the prime-distance graph on N in natural order; each vertex has finitely many earlier neighbors, so a new color always exists.
